Mapping

GIAC GAIPS mapping

GAIPS is the most direct external benchmark we found for AI platform security. This page shows which lessons relate to its published domains, and where we are not there yet.

Open the live course

Not a preparation guarantee. This is Intellica’s own reading of public domain headings. We are not affiliated with GIAC, and no level replaces or predicts the result of the exam. Confirm the current objectives, format and rules with GIAC.

What GIAC publishes

Checked 2026-11-24.

Availability
General purchase from 28 July 2026
Format
Multiple choice plus hands-on CyberLive questions, proctored, open book. GIAC says length and structure may change.
Domains
Eight, per the affiliated SANS course page
Validity
Four years from the public release, per the beta FAQ

The SANS page lists 54 questions in 2 hours with a 65% pass mark. Treat figures as indicative until confirmed with GIAC.

Priority uplift

Two domains are thin and get new lessons and labs first: development pipelines and MLOps security (Model pipelines: data, training, registry and signing) and model customisation and alignment (Fine-tuning, adapters and alignment: poisoning, backdoors and limits). We will not describe the academy as complete for GAIPS from topic titles alone. Each domain needs measurable outcomes, original lab evidence, original practice items and an independent review.

Other GIAC AI exams

Blueprint v2 benchmarked only GAIPS. GIAC now lists several AI-focused exams.

  • GAIPT (AI Penetration Tester): seven published objectives including agents, orchestration and MCP servers. It is the closest offensive benchmark, so Level 5 maps to it.
  • GASAE (AI Security Automation Engineer): automation across offensive, defensive and cloud security operations.
  • GOAA (Offensive AI Analyst): ten published objectives on offensive AI techniques.

Reviewed 2026-11-24. Intellica is independent of GIAC, ISC2, ISACA, CompTIA, CSA, IAPP, OWASP, MITRE and NIST. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published objectives. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
